name: 61 cm Type 93
_warheadComment: Mass of the explosive charge. What matters for damage is not the torpedo but this: a 490 kg Type 93 warhead does very roughly twice the structural damage of a 280 kg G7a, and no amount of torpedo defence makes that difference go away.
_settingsComment: Torpedoes were set before launch, trading speed against range. A fast setting gives the target less time to comb the tracks; a slow one lets you shoot from outside her gun range.
_wakelessComment: Steam torpedoes left a visible track a lookout could spot and a ship could turn to comb. Oxygen and electric torpedoes did not, which is most of why the Type 93 was so feared.
_armingComment: A torpedo will not detonate before it has run this far from the tube.
notes: The Long Lance. Oxygen-fuelled, so it left no wake, and it carried a heavier warhead further and faster than anything the Allies had. It also made the ships carrying it dangerously flammable: a hit among the reloads destroyed several Japanese cruisers.
